d: M42 delivers comprehensive healthcare services across the full continuum of care; from primary care to advanced specialty treatments. Leveraging cutting-edge health technologies and precision medicine, we ensure the highest standards of effectiveness, efficiency, and patient-centered outcomes. With a global presence spanning more than 480 facilities in 27 countries and a dedicated workforce of over 20,000 professionals, M42 is uniquely positioned to redefine the future of healthcare on a global scale.

Sheikh Sultan bin Zayed Hospital is a state-of-the-art hospital serving Northern Emirates. With 200+ beds and JCI accreditation, it delivers world-class, community-focused care. By leveraging cutting-edge technologies and the expertise of M42’s renowned network (including Imperial College London Diabetes Centre, Amana Healthcare, Mubadala Health Dubai, and Healthpoint), SSBZH stands at the forefront of medical innovation. The hospital is dedicated to improving health outcomes, facilitating access to quality care and addressing the unique needs of military personnel, their families, and the broader community in the Northern Emirates.

The Registered Nurse - Post Acute Rehabilitation is responsible in providing specialized nursing care to patients recovering from illness, injury, surgery, or neurological conditions, supporting rehabilitation, functional independence, and safe discharge through collaboration with the multidisciplinary team.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Nursing or equivalent.
Valid medical license from Department of Health (DOH) as Registered Nurse or eligibility to get one.
2-3 years experience in Post-Acute Rehabilitation Unit.
BLS and ACLS certifications required; PALS is an advantage.
Strong critical‑thinking and decision‑making skills under pressure.
r: Adheres to M42’s policies, procedures, and regulatory standards, maintaining professionalism and confidentiality at all times.
Delivers comprehensive nursing assessments and individualized care plans for patients, with a specialty focus on long-term care to transitional care settings.
Provides advanced nursing care, close monitoring, and support for medically complex, ventilated, or severely disabled patients, ensuring best practices and patient safety.
Administers medications and assists with complex medical procedures in accordance with clinical guidelines and unit protocols.
Promotes a safe, culturally sensitive environment that maximizes patient quality of life and supports family involvement in care.
Documents care accurately and communicates effectively with the multidisciplinary team to ensure continuity and escalation of care.
Participates in quality improvement, audits, and educational initiatives to enhance patient outcomes and service delivery.
Supports staff development through supervision, feedback, and engagement in performance evaluation, scheduling, and continuous learning.
